title: Compare your offers
help: List out cost, programs, location, and campus size for each school side by side. Pick the 2-3 factors that matter most to you and weigh your options against those first.

title: Review financial aid award letters
help: Compare the actual grants and scholarships (money you don't pay back) against loans (money you do) for each school. The sticker price isn't what matters -- the net cost after aid is.

title: Visit campuses or attend virtual info sessions
help: If you haven't seen a campus in person or virtually, now's the time. Ask about class sizes, advising, and student life, not just academics.

title: Narrow down to your final choice
help: Pick the one school you're committing to. You'll need a few days of buffer before the decision deadline to actually accept and pay your deposit.

title: Formally accept your admission offer
help: Log into the school's applicant portal and click accept, or submit a signed intent-to-enroll form if that's how your school does it. This is usually separate from paying your deposit.

title: Pay your enrollment deposit
help: Check your portal for the exact amount and whether a fee waiver is available if cost is a barrier. Pay through the portal and save your confirmation.

title: Save your deposit confirmation receipt
help: Download or screenshot the payment confirmation. You may need it later if there's ever a billing dispute.

title: Decline your other offers
help: Once you've committed, let your other schools know so they can offer your spot to someone else. Usually a quick click in each portal.

title: Submit the FAFSA
help: Create your FSA ID first (you and a parent/guardian, if you're a dependent student), then fill out the FAFSA with your family's tax info. List every school you're considering so they all receive your info.

title: Review your Student Aid Report (SAR)
help: After you submit the FAFSA, you'll get a SAR summarizing what you entered. Check it for typos or errors -- a mistake here can delay your aid.

title: Submit any financial aid verification documents
help: Some students get randomly selected for verification and need to submit extra documents (like tax transcripts). Check your portal to see if this applies to you.

title: Accept or decline each part of your aid award
help: Go through your award letter line by line. You can usually accept grants/scholarships in full but choose how much loan money (if any) to actually take.

title: Complete loan entrance counseling
help: A short required online course covering how federal student loans work and your responsibilities as a borrower. Only needed if you're accepting federal loans.

title: Sign the Master Promissory Note (MPN)
help: A legal agreement to repay your federal student loans. Sign it through studentaid.gov. Only needed if you're accepting federal loans.

title: Complete placement testing
help: Take your school's math/English placement test unless your SAT/ACT scores or AP credits already exempt you. Check your portal to confirm what's required.

title: Meet with an academic advisor
help: Schedule a session to go over your intended major's requirements before you pick classes. Many schools require this before you're allowed to register.

title: Register for your first-semester classes
help: Build a balanced schedule and register during your assigned registration window. Don't wait too long -- popular sections fill up fast.

title: Send your final high school transcript
help: Request your final transcript (with graduation confirmed) from your high school counselor's office. Ask whether your college wants it electronically or by mail, then confirm it arrived.

title: Attend mandatory pre-enrollment advising
help: If your school requires a formal advising session before classes start, schedule and attend it. Bring any transfer or AP credit info with you.

title: Set up your student email and portal account
help: Activate your account with the credentials the school emailed you, and set a secure password. Check this inbox regularly -- it's where official college communication goes.

title: Register for and attend orientation
help: Sign up for a session date through your student portal. This is often where class registration actually happens, so don't skip it.

title: Submit immunization/health records
help: Get your immunization history from your doctor or school nurse and fill out the college's health form. Some schools won't let you register for classes until this is done.

title: Apply for and confirm housing
help: Submit your housing application and deposit, fill out the roommate questionnaire, and choose a meal plan if required. Confirm your room assignment before move-in.

title: Submit required waivers or forms
help: Submit your health insurance waiver (if you have other coverage) and a FERPA release if you want parents to be able to access your records.

title: Pay your tuition bill
help: Review your bill after financial aid is applied, then either pay in full or set up a payment plan before the deadline.

title: Confirm your class schedule and locate your classes
help: Double check your final schedule for conflicts, and if you can, walk your route to classes before day one so you're not scrambling the first morning.
